correctness.rationale: The four regular tetrahedron vectors yield twelve vertices w_ij with norm² 11 and exactly eighteen edges of squared length eight, from four triangle and four hexagon facets. Section vertices correspond to edges with endpoints on opposite sides of an unoriented generic central plane. In fundamental normal chamber (1,y,z), 0<z<y<1, of area π/12, exactly four vertex-sign hyperplanes cut six rational convex polygon cells with side counts 4,5,6,4,5,6. Since each sign pattern is constant on its cell, the six-cell census proves the distribution for all generic orientations. Independent 12-vertex/18-edge reconstruction, direct crossing tests at interior rational points, seven solid-angle evaluations and normalizations reproduce the three displayed probabilities. Separately, each of the 18 equal edges has endpoint angular separation arccos(7/11), so linearity gives E[N]=18 arccos(7/11)/π, matching the distributional mean. The exact finite chamber proof, not Monte Carlo, is the infinite-orientation justification.

value.rationale: The complete Haar-uniform central-section polygon-side distribution of a canonical non-centrally-symmetric Archimedean solid is a natural exact invariant. Unlike a static 18-edge graph count, six rational orientation chambers and their spherical solid angles are needed. The independent exact mean identity supplies a reproducible benchmark. This is a mathematically motivated finite classification; a general slicing theorem or paper-sized extension is not required for its value.
residual_risks: Does not determine noncentral section law, perimeter, area or biased normal distributions.

limitations: Haar central sections only and generic side counts almost surely; no arbitrary slicing offset.
